name: Pluralist democracy
summary: Pluralist democracy is a political system with more than one centre of power, in which freedom of association lets many organised groups compete and bargain, and authority goes to leaders who build electoral coalitions. Its theorists, from Madison to Robert Dahl, hold that dispersed interests, representation and divided powers keep any single faction or elite from dominating. The common good is treated as a shifting balance of competing interests resting on a minimal consensus of tolerance, not as one fixed goal.
scope: Liberal interest-group pluralism as formulated by James Madison in Federalist No. 10 and by Robert Dahl (polyarchy, Who Governs?), as summarised in reference and encyclopedia accounts. It excludes pluralism as a general moral philosophy of value plurality except where it bears on politics, and it takes no stand on economics or social issues where pluralist theory is silent, so most such answers are low-confidence inferences or neutral.

keyFigures.name: James Madison
keyFigures.role: Author of Federalist No. 10, the founding argument that competing factions in a large republic prevent domination.

keyFigures.name: Robert A. Dahl
keyFigures.role: Political scientist who developed polyarchy and the empirical theory of group pluralism in Who Governs?

sources.title: Pluralist democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition: more than one centre of power, freedom of association, and authority through electoral coalitions built by bargaining with group leaders.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Many pluralists back social democracy, but pluralism itself sets no welfare rule, so adherents lean mildly yes while allowing group bargaining to settle the design.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Pluralism is compatible with both social-democratic and conservative economics; wage policy is left to bargaining among organized interests.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dahl criticised corporate capitalism and state socialism alike, and pluralism as such takes no side on market efficiency.

public-ownership.rationale: Pluralists worry about concentrated power, so a state monopoly over whole industries is unattractive; Dahl preferred cooperatives and dispersed ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Pluralist theory is silent on tax rates; adherents range from social democrats to conservatives like Oakeshott.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are a textbook organised interest group that gives workers a voice in the competition among groups that pluralists value.

property-fundamental.rationale: Madison treats property protection as a main task of government, yet modern pluralists accept regulation, so adherents are split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Dahl worried that corporate power undermines political equality, so pluralists tend to favour checks on large firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Pluralists who lean social-democratic oppose cuts, and the theory has no dependency argument; inferred from the social-democratic wing.

worker-ownership.rationale: Dahl himself advocated worker cooperatives, but this is his personal economics rather than something all pluralists hold.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Freedom of association and expression are conditions of competitive politics, so broad surveillance sits uneasily with pluralism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No pluralist doctrine on drug law; adherents are split between liberal and conservative positions.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Polyarchy requires freedom of expression, which pushes adherents against content restrictions, though some accept limits.

strong-leader.rationale: The whole pluralist design spreads power so no single actor can dominate; a leader bypassing gridlock inverts that.

state-harmful.rationale: Pluralist democracy depends on a state that sustains elections and guarantees associational freedom, so abolition is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Pluralism has no stated position on firearms; adherents divide along ordinary partisan lines.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pluralists favour limited, accountable coercive power, but the theory is not about security budgets; mild inference.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by pluralist theory; adherents are split.

decide-locally.rationale: Madison argued for a large republic with many interests, while pluralists also value dispersed centres of power, so neither extreme fits.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is outside pluralist theory and adherents vary.

traditional-family.rationale: Pluralism values diversity of lifestyles and convictions, so a single privileged family form is mildly rejected.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Pluralism endorses coexistence of differing lifestyles; support is inferred from that, not from stated doctrine.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pluralism treats this as a value conflict to be settled by democratic bargaining, not by doctrine.

more-religion-public.rationale: Pluralists need only minimal mutual tolerance among groups; a larger public role for one religion cuts against equal standing of all.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Connolly-style pluralization favours recognition of new identities, but classic group pluralism does not mandate active correction.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A philosophical claim outside the political theory; adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pluralism values diversity within a minimal consensus, so it neither embraces nor rejects cultural preservation.

gradual-change.rationale: Pluralists favour institutions built pragmatically on existing structures and bargaining, which implies incremental change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration levels are not addressed by pluralist theory.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pluralist theory is about domestic power distribution and gives no guidance on supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is a matter on which competing interest groups bargain; the theory takes no side.

nation-first.rationale: No stated position; pluralism concerns internal power structure rather than foreign policy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Outside the scope of pluralist theory; adherents are split.

open-borders.rationale: Pluralist democracy presumes a defined citizen body whose groups bargain, so open borders is not a natural fit; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: No pluralist doctrine on growth; environmental policy is left to group competition.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Pluralists see policy as a bargained outcome among interests, not a mandate for drastic action; no stated position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; energy policy is for group bargaining.

revolution-justified.rationale: Pluralists prefer dialogue and the peaceful balancing of interests over extremism and coercion.

experts-over-public.rationale: Dahl's pluralism limits citizens to tasks they can do reasonably well but keeps bargaining and elections, not expert rule, as the decision route.

central-planning.rationale: Dahl criticised state socialism as undemocratic because it concentrates economic power.

socialized-markets.rationale: Dahl endorsed worker-owned firms in a competitive market, but other pluralists are indifferent.

land-value-tax.rationale: No pluralist position on the tax base.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a welfare design question for group bargaining.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariffs are a classic subject of interest-group bargaining, on which the theory itself is neutral.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Concentrating investment decisions in the state conflicts with dispersing centres of power; inferred from Dahl's wariness of concentrated economic power.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Madison and Dahl both favour many dispersed interests; wide ownership fits that, though it is not a stated programme.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing the market economy is far outside any pluralist programme and would end independent organised interests.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in pluralist theory, so adherents have no shared view on abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Pluralism is usually contrasted with corporatism: groups compete freely rather than being state-recognised, so adherents resist the statist version though group bargaining is central.

one-party-rule.rationale: A system with more than one centre of power and competing electoral coalitions excludes single-party rule by definition.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Pluralism does not require a republic; Oakeshott-style conservative pluralists accept monarchy, others do not.

democracy-best.rationale: Modern democracies are pluralist by definition and adherents regard competitive democracy as the fair way to balance interests.

direct-votes.rationale: Madison argued pure democracy lacks any cure for majority faction and representation filters opinion; pluralists favour representative bargaining.

workers-councils.rationale: Pluralist democracy is built on competing parties, elections and many groups, not on a single class council system.

natural-rulers.rationale: Dahl's account of equality presumes that all citizens' preferences count equally, rejecting natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Pluralism favours good-faith dialogue over coercion and extremism, but the sources do not discuss pacifism as such.

war-builds-character.rationale: Pluralists stress dialogue and tolerance, so glorifying war is alien; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Pluralists differ; some accept establishment so long as religious diversity is tolerated.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Pluralism is about coexistence of many convictions, which scriptural lawmaking by one faith would override.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Pluralist democracy presumes a state that guarantees associational freedom and rules; private provision is not part of it.

military-superiority.rationale: Foreign policy is outside the theory.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Pluralism rests on diversity of groups within one political body, so an ethnically uniform nation is not its ideal.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Pluralists see many cross-cutting interests rather than a single decisive class conflict; Marxism is called too rigid.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Dahl's concern is political equality and voting equality, not equal material outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No stated position; treated as a group-claims question for the democratic process.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations between states are not part of pluralist theory, and adherents would treat the claim as a matter for ordinary political bargaining.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unification by civilization is not part of pluralist theory and cuts against internal diversity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Madison accepts self-interest as a given and builds institutions around it, without calling it a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Polyarchy rests on individual political rights such as expression and association, which pluralists would not subordinate to duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is outside pluralist political theory.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is outside pluralist theory, so there is no shared position on limiting growth.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Pluralism rejects utopian and historicist narratives of this kind; mild inference.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed, though pluralists prefer pragmatic institutional change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is a bioethics issue that pluralist theory does not address, so adherents split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Pluralist democracy runs on elections and group bargaining among people, so handing decisions to algorithms is mildly rejected.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; though associational freedom hints at support, doctrine is silent.

restore-past-order.rationale: Pluralists reject historicism and fixed visions of the good; progress or restoration is not their organising aim.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pluralists reject rigid single ideologies and favour pragmatic institutions and balancing of values.

direct-action.rationale: Pluralist theory has leaders winning authority through electoral coalitions and bargaining, treating elections as the main channel.

means-match-ends.rationale: Pluralism says nothing on whether methods must mirror aims, so this is left neutral.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Pluralist democracy relies on many specialised organised groups, which presupposes a division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution is left to bargaining among groups; a single distributive principle of this kind is not pluralist.

production-for-use.rationale: Dahl criticised both capitalism and state socialism; no common position among pluralists.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory is a single rigid ideology that pluralists reject.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class with dictatorial power contradicts a system with more than one centre of power and freedom of association.

collective-farming.rationale: No pluralist position; compulsory collective forms conflict with diversity of ownership.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pluralists reject single-cause historical theories of this type.

taxation-theft.rationale: Madison saw regulating the clash of interests, including through taxation, as a principal task of legislation, not a theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Pluralists value tolerance of diverse lifestyles but accept varied limits; no stated rule.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Interest-group pluralism makes organised groups the main political actors, so rights and representation are not purely individual.

conscription.rationale: Military service is not covered by pluralist theory, and adherents differ on compulsory service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Polyarchy defines democracy by elections and participation, so voice is the main check, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Dahl's pluralism treats citizens as participants in group bargaining, not customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Dahl's emphasis on effective participation implies some resource conditions, but pluralists differ.

media-academia-power.rationale: Dahl argued against claims that one elite rules; the claim here posits a concentrated hidden power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dahl's premise of equal standing of citizens opposes racial hierarchy; the empirical claim is not addressed.

organic-representation.rationale: Pluralist democracy has representation via territorial elections and competing leaders of organisations, while organic estate models give fixed corporate seats.

total-state.rationale: A system with multiple centres of power and free association is the opposite of a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Pluralists distrust utopian projects of radical renewal and favour pragmatic institutional adaptation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority via oaths between lords and followers is incompatible with authority gained through electoral coalitions.

bound-labor.rationale: Legal bondage contradicts the equal standing and freedom of association that polyarchy requires.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Pluralists value dialogue among differing convictions but do not make power-relativism of knowledge a doctrine.

universal-morality.rationale: Pluralism holds that value plurality cannot be reduced to one rationally derived code; this reading is inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: The common good is described as a shifting balance of competing interests, not one good fixed by reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Pluralist theory takes no stand on Zionism or any particular national state, so there is no inferable position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return rights for diasporas are not addressed by pluralist theory, so no position is inferable.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not addressed by pluralist theory, which only values diversity in general terms.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Dahl argued for workplace democracy and worker-owned firms, though other pluralists do not share it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is outside the theory.

economic-freedom.rationale: Madison links liberty and property, but Dahl called for limits on corporate power; adherents split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Madison's design assumes rulers are not angels and relies on institutional checks rather than moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Pluralist theory concerns power inside a political body, not the right of nations to separate states, so it stays neutral.

force-without-un.rationale: Authorisation of force abroad is a foreign-policy question outside pluralist theory.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Pluralism tolerates diverse convictions, including religious ones, and does not make reason the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants is not addressed by pluralist theory, and adherents split along ordinary lines.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; welfare conditions are subject to group bargaining.

class-collaboration.rationale: Pluralists favour bargaining and good-faith dialogue among interest groups over sharpened class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Pluralists value diverse inherited institutions and reject sweeping destruction in the name of an ideology.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts of states are outside pluralist theory about domestic power distribution.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organise nationally or internationally is not a pluralist question, so no position is inferable.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Pluralism values equal political standing and diversity of lifestyles; legal role assignments are mildly rejected.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; economic pluralism would not endorse a religious ban imposed on all.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Polyarchy requires equal political rights for all citizens, which is incompatible with legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Dahl argued against the claim that a single power elite or class rules, holding that competing groups share influence.

proportional-representation.rationale: Pluralists differ on electoral systems; both PR and plurality arrangements fit.

national-mission.rationale: Pluralism stresses tolerance and not imposing one form on others, though the doctrine is silent on foreign policy.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed by classical pluralism, though Connolly-style pluralization would sympathise.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Dahl defended the competitive responsiveness of polyarchy against elite-rule claims, so a blanket charge is rejected.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State coercion over reproduction violates the equal rights polyarchy presupposes.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Legal accountability for past abuses is not discussed in the sources, so adherents are treated as split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Pluralists accept an active state; many support social democracy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Pluralism values coexistence across diverse groups; state discouragement of this conflicts with equal rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Voting equality and equal consideration of citizens' preferences are the foundation of Dahl's democratic criteria.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal debate of Marxism-Leninism that pluralist theory does not engage.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Whether settler states count as colonial is a historiographic question pluralist theory does not address.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Pluralists may allow group-based legal arrangements or uniform law; the theory is open.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Pluralism rests on freedom of belief and association for all groups.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious ban imposed on all would override diversity of convictions.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Pluralism keeps churches as independent groups, but the theory does not settle the extent of state regulation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority in pluralist democracy is gained through electoral coalitions, which implies a consent basis though the theory emphasises bargaining.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims for the trade balance are not part of pluralist theory, which treats trade as one interest-group issue.

population-transfer.rationale: Coerced removal of a minority violates the equal rights and freedom of association of polyarchy.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian absolute not addressed by pluralist theory.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Madison relies on competition among factions as a safeguard, but not as an engine of progress between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Pluralism needs minimal consensus and warns against extremism, but banning parties conflicts with freedom of association; adherents are split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not stated, although preventing any faction dominating is Madison's concern.

separated-powers.rationale: Madison's Federalist argument is that dividing power and multiplying interests keeps any one faction from dominating, and pluralism defines itself by more than one centre of power.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined vanguard monopoly contradicts competing electoral coalitions and multiple centres of power.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Pluralism sets no priority among social groups, instead treating policy as a bargain among competing interests, so it stays neutral.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is a distributional question settled by group bargaining, with no pluralist doctrine on it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Freedom of association and group competition supports union action; restrictions are mildly opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The causes of poverty are an empirical dispute pluralist theory does not take sides on.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Pluralism holds that diversity within a political body can coexist given a minimal consensus of tolerance.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Pluralist theory is built on offices won through electoral coalitions, not on random selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Polyarchy requires continuing rights such as expression and association, so suspension is mildly rejected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are a policy matter for bargaining among interests, and pluralist theory itself is silent.

party-controls-media.rationale: Dahl's polyarchy lists freedom of expression and alternative sources of information among its required institutions, which government control of media would remove.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party commanding the army concentrates power in a single centre, contradicting pluralism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are not addressed by pluralist theory, and adherents have no shared view.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not addressed by pluralist theory, which offers no shared position.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parties as electoral coalitions use some discipline, but the theory does not demand it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Madison's separation of powers favours dividing military and legislative control; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Internal church governance is the business of independent religious groups, on which pluralist theory takes no side.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by one religious authority is a single centre of power and denies equal footing to other convictions.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Marxist position about inter-imperialist war that pluralist theory does not address.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Freedom of expression is a required institution of polyarchy and a pluralist society of diverse convictions.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Madison's concern with concentrated power implies unease about permanent incumbency; not directly stated.

recall-officials.rationale: Pluralists differ; recall is not part of the core theory.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is a foreign-policy matter outside pluralist theory.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; mandated single tenure form would conflict with diversity of arrangements.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militia versus professional army is not addressed by pluralist theory, so adherents are treated as split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The moral comparison of rural and urban life is outside pluralist political theory.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided nations is a nationalist question pluralist theory does not address.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Pluralism favours dialogue across groups and does not accept group-based contempt.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Pluralism values coexistence but does not claim cultural relativism.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is a value dispute that pluralism leaves to democratic bargaining rather than settling by doctrine.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; pluralist toleration of belief does not extend to science curricula; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pluralism offers no rule on pornography law, and adherents split between liberal and conservative views.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules by descent or birth are not discussed in the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Pluralism values diversity of groups within one body; support is inferred rather than stated.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Pluralists differ on exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A Millian position outside pluralist political theory.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief for poor countries is an international economics issue outside pluralist theory.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Whether political independence requires economic transformation is a anti-colonial debate pluralist theory does not engage.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Polyarchy treats political freedoms as definitional, so trading them for growth is rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Duties of aid between countries are outside pluralist theory, which concerns domestic power distribution.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear force posture is a defence-policy question outside pluralist theory.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Pluralists accept both parliamentary and presidential forms.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The sources on pluralism do not discuss central bank independence, so adherents are treated as split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions in peace deals are outside pluralist theory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The common good is a shifting balance for pluralists, with no stated property doctrine.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The classification of the Soviet economy is a Marxist dispute that pluralist theory does not address.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk standards are a policy matter for group bargaining, with no pluralist doctrine on them.

collective-defense.rationale: Treaty commitments of mutual defence are outside pluralist theory.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legal status of annexed territories is an international-law question outside pluralist theory.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; both ceremonial and partisan heads fit pluralist democracy.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Pluralist theory does not address whether force may stop secession, so adherents are treated as split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-status arrangements for regions are not covered by pluralist theory.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred ruler would be a single unchallengeable centre of power, the reverse of pluralism.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is a distributional issue left to interest-group bargaining, with no pluralist rule.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is an empirical question outside political pluralism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Madison's whole scheme aims at controlling power by institutional checks, so a ruler above the law is rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is outside pluralist theory.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Madison's republic combines representation, extended sphere and divided powers to balance interests, a close cousin of mixed government, though pluralists do not endorse rule by the few.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass veneration of one leader belongs with concentration of power that pluralists reject.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are family-law policy that pluralist theory does not address.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist doctrine pluralists regard as too rigid; not directly addressed.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; interest-group conflict would settle it.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not covered by the sources on pluralism, so no position is inferable.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not addressed; claims based on nationality of kin abroad conflict with a diversity-based view.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of conviction and association is central to pluralism.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelling a single dress code overrides pluralism's tolerance of differing lifestyles.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are an economic-integration matter on which pluralist theory is silent.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political union of related peoples is a pan-nationalist idea pluralist theory does not address.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Self-governing cultural groups fit group pluralism, though classical pluralism does not discuss it explicitly.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The strategy of a persecuted minority is not addressed by pluralist theory, though group organisation within a state fits its outlook.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Pluralists reject single-factor historical determinism like Marxism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Dahl worried about concentrations of economic power, and competition rules preserve many centres of power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is an economic-policy matter the pluralist sources do not discuss.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Pluralists favour institutions that balance competing principles, which includes checks on majorities; Madison feared majority faction.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for public bodies are a representation question on which pluralists split, as the sources give no rule.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are outside pluralist theory.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade deals are a policy matter that pluralist theory leaves to group bargaining.

moral-incentives.rationale: Pluralism relies on the bargaining of interests rather than moral mobilisation; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Pluralists prefer dialogue and reject coercion and extremism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equality of citizens' standing in Dahl's criteria implies no hereditary political privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History curriculum framing is not discussed in the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Dahl's equal-standing premise tells against permanent rule over others; not directly addressed.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotic education is not addressed by pluralist theory, and adherents differ.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a policy dispute on which pluralist theory takes no side.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is outside pluralist theory.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism can avoid collapse is a Marxist debate that pluralist theory does not engage.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence policy is a foreign-policy question outside pluralist theory.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory strategies for poor countries are outside pluralist theory.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist concept that pluralists, who reject single-class frameworks, would not adopt.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Pluralists differ on how far freedom of association extends in the market.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Madison's design controls majority faction by institutions, and polyarchy requires secured freedoms, but pluralists also accept parliamentary systems.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The legal force of colonial treaties is an international-law question that pluralist theory does not address.

elective-rulers.rationale: Authority comes through successful electoral coalitions, so rulers are chosen by election.

minority-veto.rationale: Madison feared both majority and minority factions, so a single dissenter's veto is rejected, though consensus protections are valued.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Constitutional checks on rulers are central to Madison's design; the resistance right is inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Madison's separation of powers diverges from parliamentary supremacy, but pluralists accept parliamentary systems.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is a moral question outside political pluralism.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use for food and research is a moral and policy question pluralism leaves to group competition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duties of the privileged are a conservative ethical idea that the pluralist sources do not discuss.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Dahl's democracy requires effective participation of citizens through groups, so withdrawal is discouraged.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim that pluralists do not adopt.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Dahl argued that no single ruling class holds power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems analysis is an economic-theory claim pluralist theory does not address.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal political standing of citizens implies no native-born office restrictions; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Autonomy among communist parties is an internal Marxist-Leninist matter outside pluralist theory.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is outside pluralist theory.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands are a foreign-policy question outside pluralist theory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Reserved leadership conflicts with voting equality as Dahl states it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Whether a constitution should enshrine anti-fascism is not addressed by the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Both concentrate power in one centre and abolish competing groups, so pluralists condemn them together; inferred from the definition.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical question outside the theory.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is a cultural dispute for democratic bargaining, with no pluralist rule.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Which social disadvantages deserve attention is a contested policy question pluralism leaves to group competition.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: This empirical and policy dispute lies outside pluralist theory.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Pluralists hold that democratic pluralism is a general approach, not culturally bound, though it should be built on local historical structures.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A military with a political guardian role becomes a rival centre of power outside electoral competition, which pluralism does not accept.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognition of unpaid care as labour is a feminist economic demand the pluralist sources do not address.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations are a cultural ethic outside political pluralism.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examination-based recruitment is not discussed in the pluralist sources, and pluralists do not specify civil-service rules.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign ownership screening is an economic-policy matter pluralist theory does not address.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is a family-policy question for democratic bargaining, with no pluralist doctrine.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Pluralist leaders bargain across groups and win office through coalitions, which a binding mandate would restrict.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is a welfare-policy matter outside pluralist theory.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; communal-only tenure removes diversity of ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Dividing power between executive and legislature is Madison's remedy, and legislative control of money is a standard check.

single-official-language.rationale: Official language policy is not addressed directly by the pluralist sources, and adherents are treated as split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Restrictions on foreign land ownership are a property policy matter outside pluralist theory.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal tests for discrimination are not addressed in the pluralist sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The cultural critique of consumption is not part of pluralist political theory.

corporate-influence.rationale: Dahl and critics of pluralism both worried about corporate weight in politics, and the SEP reports the critique that powerful economic interests organise and benefit most.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert support for foreign insurgents is a foreign-policy question outside pluralist theory.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Great-power interventions in allied states are outside pluralist theory.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Freedom of association is a polyarchy condition, so restrictions on groups' funding are mildly resisted.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth-rate policy is a demographic matter outside pluralist theory.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency limits on property purchases are not addressed in the pluralist sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: A federal job guarantee is a macroeconomic policy proposal pluralist theory neither backs nor opposes.

democratic-peace.rationale: Pluralists favour democracy, but the sources do not discuss the democratic peace thesis.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The philosophical question of political obligation is not addressed by the pluralist sources.

non-intervention.rationale: Non-intervention between states is an international-relations principle outside pluralist theory.

industrial-unions.rationale: The craft versus industrial union question is an internal labour-movement matter outside pluralist theory.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Pluralism rests on good-faith dialogue and mutual respect among groups, which conspiracy accusations against a minority violate.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Legal marriage reform is not addressed in the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Alternative sources of information are an institution of Dahl's polyarchy, supporting open government information.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is not part of pluralist political theory.

informal-organisation.rationale: Pluralist theory expects organised groups led by identifiable leaders in electoral coalitions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Precedence of domestic over international law is not addressed in the pluralist sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the community by one religion contradicts pluralism's co-existence of convictions.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; ritual submission is alien to pluralist equal standing.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not addressed in the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The line between personal belongings and productive property is a socialist formulation outside pluralist theory.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War strategy toward communism is a foreign-policy matter outside pluralist theory.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Pluralists favour dispersed institutions built pragmatically, which fits mixed provision; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Pluralism tolerates religious convictions and does not frame belief as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist historical role of capitalism is not something pluralist theory takes up.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Whether women's equality requires economic transformation is a socialist-feminist claim pluralist theory does not address.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialising housework is a socialist-feminist demand outside pluralist theory.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; language policing conflicts with pluralism's openness.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations inside a state are not addressed in the pluralist sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Dahl liked cooperatives, but a total reorganisation into communes is not pluralist.

majority-settlement.rationale: State engineering of minority regions conflicts with pluralism's respect for group diversity and equal rights.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Dahl criticised both, but pluralists do not generally claim a third system.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing claims to land by history or religion are outside pluralist theory.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Pluralism requires a minimal consensus of mutual respect, and denial is hostile to it; the factual claim is rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Pluralism values coexistence of differing lifestyles and rejects coercive suppression of a minority.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Dahl's polyarchy requires free and fair competitive elections and freedom of association, and suppression of opposition removes both.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Pluralism protects diverse convictions and does not endorse state punishment of one religion's critics.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Equal standing of those governed is the democratic premise; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is a point of Islamic jurisprudence outside pluralist theory.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Pluralism favours peaceful dialogue and rejects forcible removal for religious reasons.

participatory-democracy.rationale: SEP notes pluralism is not particularly compatible with deliberative direct participation; bargaining among groups is its method.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Connolly-type pluralization sympathises, but classical pluralism does not discuss it.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Legal gender recognition is a contested social policy that classical pluralism does not address.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is a moral dispute that pluralism leaves to democratic bargaining, with no rule of its own.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Pluralists seek balance of competing values but do not declare the spectrum obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept that pluralists treat as one rigid ideology.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Pluralism rests on coexistence among diverse convictions and mutual respect.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority in pluralist democracy is built through electoral coalitions, not from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents differ on state neutrality and religious expression.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment contract rules on NDAs are not addressed in the pluralist sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Many pluralists support social democracy, which fits market economy plus social protection; not a stated rule.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Abolishing armies is a pacifist demand outside pluralist theory.

rich-first.rationale: Uneven growth strategies are a development-economics question outside pluralist theory.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Non-alignment is a foreign-policy matter outside pluralist theory.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Office by inheritance bypasses electoral coalition-building that pluralist democracy relies on.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit schemes are outside pluralist theory.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Conditionality on international loans is an economic-policy dispute outside pluralist theory.

property-franchise.rationale: Dahl's criteria require voting equality and an inclusive citizenship, which a property franchise violates.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is outside the classical pluralist sources.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Lukacsian theory; pluralists reject single rigid ideologies.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Dahl's critics highlight this point, but pluralists generally hold press freedom is real; split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Madison's remedy for faction is a government of institutions and rule of law; inferred as rule through standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Dahl's definition of polyarchy requires inclusive citizenship and voting equality, so racial limits are excluded.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation methods are not discussed in the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

open-government-data.rationale: Information access is a polyarchy condition; support for open records is an inference.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: State restrictions on marriage across faiths conflict with pluralism's tolerance.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority's businesses violates the mutual respect pluralists require between groups.

citizens-assembly.rationale: SEP says pluralism is not particularly compatible with deliberative public justification, and random selection replaces elections.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Doctrinal reform is an internal question for religious groups, on which pluralist theory takes no side.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Dahl feared concentrated economic power as a threat to political equality, and Madison saw unequal property as a durable source of faction.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military personnel policy is not addressed in the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Pluralism tolerates all convictions, so state promotion of atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Pluralist democracy presupposes a state that enforces rules and guarantees associational freedom.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Pluralism favours institutions that reflect and balance competing groups, which power-sharing does in divided societies.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Private versus public poor relief is not addressed in the pluralist sources, and adherents split along economic lines.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not a pluralist device; Dahl limits citizens to tasks they can do reasonably well.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Long-term risk prioritisation is outside pluralist theory.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; religious groups govern themselves.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Equal standing of persons implies shared marital authority; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights of non-citizens are not discussed in the pluralist sources, so no position is inferable.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are a distributional housing policy settled by group bargaining, with no pluralist rule.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property reform is outside pluralist theory.

uniformed-youth.rationale: State-run drilled youth movements are a means of concentrated control that pluralism rejects in favour of independent groups.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing of nuclear weapons is a defence-policy matter outside pluralist theory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is a foreign-policy question outside pluralist theory.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal recognition of past genocides is a politics-of-memory question pluralism does not address.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Whether income should reward labour over ownership is a distributive principle the pluralist sources do not adopt.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; pacifism is not part of pluralism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Pluralists reject historicist myths; mild inference.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The theoretical claim about sex is outside political pluralism.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Connolly-type pluralization sympathises, but classical pluralism is silent.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring national martyrs is a nationalist cultural practice not addressed by pluralist theory.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Pluralism treats politics as balancing competing interests through dialogue, not a struggle of good against evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The role of a homeland for its diaspora is a nationalist question outside pluralist theory.

culture-before-state.rationale: The cultural-nationalist ordering of renewal and statehood is outside pluralist theory.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is an internal question for religious groups, outside pluralist theory.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is an internal religious debate outside pluralist theory.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Reserving economic life to one group violates pluralism's equal standing of groups.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Redrawing administrative regions around a people is a nationalist demand outside pluralist theory.

independent-unions.rationale: Independent organised groups competing for influence are the core of the pluralist model, and unions are a standard example.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The criterion for calling a society socialist is a Marxist dispute outside pluralist theory.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of local utilities is a policy matter on which pluralist theory is silent.

second-chamber.rationale: Madison's scheme multiplies checks between bodies and filters opinion, and pluralists favour institutions that balance competing principles.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipalist ownership models are outside pluralist theory.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian-municipalist confederation is a specific anarchist-leaning model that pluralist theory does not address.

family-wage.rationale: The family wage is not addressed in the pluralist sources, so it stays neutral.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation speed is a regulatory-policy question outside pluralist theory.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Research funding priorities are outside pluralist theory.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payment traceability is a privacy-policy matter that the pluralist sources do not address.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is not discussed in the pluralist sources, though associational freedom hints at sympathy.

person-over-state.rationale: Polyarchy's equal citizenship and protected rights imply this; the wording is not directly stated.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The claim about a spiritual human nature is metaphysical and outside political pluralism.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The sources on pluralism do not settle whether regional powers may be revoked, so adherents are treated as split.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural technology is a policy dispute for group bargaining, with no pluralist rule.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form is an environmental-planning claim outside pluralist theory.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Interest-group pluralism accepts organised groups, but racial-bloc organising is not a defining stance; mild inference.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is a cultural attitude outside the pluralist sources, so adherents are treated as split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Limits on the use of force are a foreign-policy doctrine outside pluralist theory.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pluralism takes diverse groups as living in one political body; mildly rejected.

communal-electorates.rationale: Pluralist democracy forms coalitions across groups at general elections, not separate rolls; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed; conspiracy framing conflicts with good-faith dialogue.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is a distributional question settled by group bargaining, with no pluralist rule.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not addressed by pluralist theory and is left to group bargaining.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Pluralism values diversity within a minimal consensus of tolerance, so demanding that newcomers give up their culture is mildly rejected.

elite-replacement.rationale: Pluralism rests on good-faith dialogue and mutual respect among groups, and this conspiracy claim against elites and immigrants breaches that.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Pluralists reject strengthening a single concentrated state centre as a permanent doctrine; the Marxist-Leninist question is not addressed.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Pluralists differ on how constitutions are rewritten; the theory is silent.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pluralism sets no policy instrument; environmental policy is left to bargaining among organised interests.

future-generations.rationale: Pluralist theory is about present competing interests and sets no duty to future generations; adherents hold varied views.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Pluralism welcomes group representation but makes no claim about women's distinct values; adherents split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Defence levels are left to group bargaining and electoral coalitions, with no pluralist rule.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Pluralist theory is about domestic power dispersal and does not settle secrecy in treaties, though openness fits free association.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic policy is compatible with both social-democratic and conservative views, so adherents split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Dahl's polyarchy assumes a state able to keep order and control coercion so that competing groups play by peaceful rules; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Pluralist theory assumes civilian control and lawful order within the state; it does not endorse refusal; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Pluralism holds that organised groups bargain with each other and government, which fits union bargaining; inferred from freedom of association.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Pluralist theory sets no welfare rule and leaves the design to group bargaining.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; pluralists leave fiscal policy to the bargaining of competing interests.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Pluralist theory is a domestic account and takes no stand on the global economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pluralist democracy works through existing institutions, divided powers and electoral coalitions, so destroying the state machinery is opposed.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Rejecting a single fixed goal and valuing many centres of power fit open experimentation; Dahl also wrote on economic democracy; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Treating the common good as a shifting balance of interests resting on tolerance leaves no room for a sacred nation.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; pluralism concerns competing groups, not regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Madison's Federalist No. 10 refers to human nature as source of faction but does not address dignity or redesign; adherents split.

public-service-media.rationale: Dahl lists alternative, independent sources of information as a condition of polyarchy, so independent public media fit; public funding is an inference.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Political pluralism treats religious diversity as something to tolerate under a minimal consensus, and takes no stand on whether religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy is a classic case of group bargaining; pluralism itself takes no side on price supports.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Pluralist theory does not address nuclear arms policy, so adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Freedom of association lets workers organise their own party, and polyarchy requires the freedom to form parties and groups; inferred as a mild yes, since coalition-building also works through broad parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: A pluralist polity rests on equal rights and tolerance; a ban on this violation of bodily integrity is inferred, but pluralism does not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Dahl's polyarchy rests on political equality of citizens, so equal legal property rights for women are inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Pluralist theory has no position on language classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Pluralists expect rules to emerge from bargaining among organised groups, including regulators and interest groups, rather than reliance on private lawsuits alone; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Madison and Dahl place lawmaking in elected representatives and divided offices; a formal seat for unelected customary leaders is inferred to be unwelcome.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Pluralism prizes liberty and association as the safeguard against domination, so it would not give priority to environmental goals over liberty; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Separation of powers and judicial independence, which Madison defends, suggest judges keep sentencing discretion; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Pluralism stresses a minimal consensus of tolerance and takes no stand on language requirements, so adherents are split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Unions are one organised group among many in pluralist theory, but the theory sets no rule on union membership, and adherents split between labour-friendly and business-friendly views.

voter-id.rationale: Polyarchy requires inclusive citizenship and free, fair elections, but nothing in pluralist theory settles identification rules, and adherents differ on access versus integrity.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Pluralism rests on a minimal consensus of tolerance among diverse groups, from which equal legal standing for religious interpretations is inferred; the sources do not address it directly.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Dahl defines polyarchy by a set of procedural institutions, chiefly free and fair competitive elections, and pluralist democracy is defined by competition and bargaining, not by outcomes; some adherents add substantive conditions such as association rights.

premarital-sex.rationale: Pluralism is silent on sexual morals; its tolerance of diverse ways of life is the basis for a mild inference that adherents accept it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Polyarchy requires freedom of expression and access to alternative information, so blanket shutdowns cut against its required institutions; the sources do not mention the internet.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Pluralism sets no welfare design, and its adherents range from social democrats to conservatives, so group bargaining is left to settle it.

women-suffrage.rationale: Dahl's polyarchy requires inclusive citizenship and equal voting rights for adults, which covers women's right to vote and hold office.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Pluralist theory does not treat religion as a source of oppression and is tolerant of religious groups as legitimate associations; this is inferred from that tolerance.

race-social-construct.rationale: Pluralist theory does not address race as a category; mainstream adherents likely accept the scholarly consensus, which is inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Pluralists accept groups pressing the state for such bodies but the theory prescribes no agencies, and adherents split on state action.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Pluralism sets no rule for property origins; it treats property as one of many interests that groups bargain over.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Theory concerns domestic power dispersal; adherents lean liberal but the sources give no view on international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: its minimal consensus of tolerance and many competing groups sits against one doctrine ruling public life, but it takes no view on scripture itself.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: its emphasis on inclusive participation of many groups in bargaining favours guaranteed participation, though Indigenous governance is not discussed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: a single bureaucracy controlling the economy concentrates power, which pluralists oppose, though the question was not addressed.

indirect-election.rationale: Dahl's polyarchy requires officials elected in free and fair elections with broad participation, favouring direct popular choice, though Madison accepted filtering through representation.

national-church-status.rationale: Pluralism rests on freedom of association among many groups competing on equal terms, which counts against a legally privileged church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: dispersing power among territorial and group centres fits pluralism, and Madison's extended republic favoured divided authority; the sources do not address ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its democratic commitment to inhabitants' participation; the sources do not discuss territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by the theory, which concerns power within an established polity.

simple-living.rationale: Pluralist theory is silent on lifestyle; adherents hold varied views.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; group protection and open association pull in opposite directions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; the theory takes no position on military service.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Pluralism concerns competing groups in politics; a shared spiritual tie to land is not part of it, so inferred mildly negative.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Polyarchy depends on civil liberties and the rule of law, which are incompatible with state killing without trial; drug policy itself is not discussed.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment is outside pluralist theory; neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not addressed by pluralist theory; neutral.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Resource ownership is outside pluralist theory and left to group bargaining.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from liberal freedom of association and individual rights; self-ownership is not discussed.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is left to bargaining among interests; the theory sets no rule.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design is left to bargaining among organised groups.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Pluralist theory holds that organised groups and parties link citizens to government, so bypassing them is the opposite of its core claim.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Madison expects factions to seek advantage and relies on checks, not a ban; the theory sets no rule on state favour for firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Freedom of association lets religious groups organise, so pluralists tolerate denominational politics; they set no rule against it.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from liberal rights and equal citizenship within democracy; family law is not discussed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Distributive theory is outside pluralism; neutral.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Madison stresses lawful procedure and checks, while liberal pluralists value conscience, so adherents split.

multipolar-world.rationale: Dahl's dispersed-power logic is domestic and he does not address the international order; neutral.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Pluralists treat the common good as a balance of interests and sit within liberal rather than Marxist economics; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not addressed; pluralism treats identity and material groups alike as interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Pluralism requires more than one centre of power and free competition among parties, so rule under one party contradicts it.

missingStatements.text: Political power should be spread among many independent organised groups rather than concentrated in one body.
missingStatements.rationale: Several centres of power are the definition of pluralist democracy, and Madison's argument for many competing factions makes dispersal the main safeguard.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be free to form independent associations, parties and interest groups to press their interests.
missingStatements.rationale: Freedom of association is the stated condition for pluralist democracy and one of Dahl's required polyarchy institutions.

notes: Pluralism is a theory of how power is distributed, so economic and social positions vary: some pluralists lean social-democratic (Dahl endorsed worker cooperatives), others conservative (Oakeshott). Most such answers are therefore neutral or low-confidence. Critics such as Domhoff and Lindblom dispute whether groups really compete on equal terms.
